newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra sees A$1 bln social security saving.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra sees A$1 bln social security saving.

text.p: Australian Social Security Minister Jocelyn Newman said Canberra would save A$1 billion in the fiscal year to June 1997 from a social security crackdown.

"A tightening of the Social Security System, with improved data matching, more frequent reviews and improved systems to prevent overpayments, will save the Australian taxpayer around a billion dollars this year," Newman said in a statement.
"An increase in reviews alone has resulted in overpayments totalling A$55.7 million being identified in the July to September quarter this year ..."
It was not immediately clear whether the money was budgeted.

However, a spokesman for the minister said the A$1 billion figure was implied by an estimate of A$384 million social security overpayments having been recovered or avoided in the first quarter of the year.
That rate of overpayment avoidance and recovery was an improvement on the previous year and to that the extent, approximately, it was also an improvement on budget estimates, he said.
The spokesman could not, however, give an immediate estimate of the unbudgeted boost.
